reason: The agent briefing and blast-radius idea is exactly what I've been hunting for, so I'd spin up the free self-hosted version on one team's repos this month. But I wouldn't put $20 per engineer per month for an early-preview hosted product in front of finance until a pilot proves it cuts the 'who owns this?' churn and catches a bad agent change.
objection: Per-seat pricing for a whole org when only a handful of people and agents actually drive the value is a hard sell to finance, and handing Slack, Drive and incident history to a hosted service that's still in early preview makes security review slow.
would_change_my_mind: Pricing per active user or per agent/repo instead of per engineer, plus a security posture (SOC 2 or a clear data-handling story) good enough to pass review, after a self-hosted pilot shows real answers with real citations.
